value.body: A staff nurse is a registered nurse who gives direct care to patients in hospital wards, ICUs, operation theatres and clinics. Employers include government and private hospitals, nursing homes and clinics. A shift involves assessing patients, giving medicines and treatments as prescribed, monitoring vital signs, keeping records and handing over to the next shift.

items.label: Typical entry
items.note: Registration with a State Nursing Council is required

items.label: Registered nursing personnel in India
items.note: All categories, including ANMs and GNMs
items.source: Indian Nursing Council figures in Parliament replies (as reported)

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Patient monitors, infusion pumps, medication charts, hospital record systems

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology, then a 4-year B.Sc Nursing through state or institution entrance tests, or the GNM diploma. After registering with the State Nursing Council, freshers join hospitals as staff nurses; government posts are filled through recruitment exams such as AIIMS NORCET and state nursing recruitment.

value.title: At a glance
items: Growth paths include senior nurse, ward in-charge and nursing supervisor; an M.Sc Nursing opens teaching and specialist roles.
Rotating shifts, including nights and weekends, are standard.
Some nurses later work abroad after clearing that country's licensing exams.

competition.note: B.Sc Nursing graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
